title: Multivariate-normal MLE with incomplete data
procedure: Maximum-likelihood estimation of the mean vector mu and covariance matrix Sigma of a multivariate normal distribution from data with arbitrary item-level missingness (missing-at-random). Each observation contributes the marginal log-likelihood over its observed coordinates; the estimator maximizes the summed observed-data log-likelihood.
algorithms: Forward-Cholesky parameterization of Sigma: the optimizer works in the unconstrained space of a Cholesky factor, so every iterate is positive-definite by construction (no projection/repair step). This is the contribution the mvnmle paper formalizes.
CPU default since 3.17.0: a fast forward-Cholesky estimator in fp64 (deterministic).
Apple-Metal (MPS) optimizer loop since 3.18.0: a single fused objective/gradient pass per iteration; GPU reductions are fp32 (mildly non-deterministic in the last digits).
Trace-term evaluation has two backends (direct solve vs blocked) selected per device; gradients via analytic form or autodiff (see the factorial study).

reference.name: R mvnmle
reference.what: The CRAN mvnmle package, which maximizes the same observed-data likelihood using an inverse-Cholesky parameterization in fp64. It is the established reference implementation; agreement in loglik and in the estimated mu/Sigma summaries (Frobenius norm, log-determinant) is the correctness claim.
also_compared: semopy (Python SEM, on the GSS survey)

tolerances.loglik_vs_r: Agreement to fp64 round-off on CPU; GPU fp32 paths agree to ~1e-4 relative on loglik and may differ in the last reported digit of mu/Sigma.
tolerances.estimate_agreement: Cross-engine agreement checked via sigma_fro and sigma_logdet rather than full elementwise equality at large p (the full p x p matrix is O(p^2) and is only stored for p <= 100).
tolerances.gpu_nondeterminism: fp32 GPU reductions are not bit-reproducible across runs; timings are reported as medians over repeats and estimates as the last timed repeat.

limitations: R mvnmle does not run past roughly p = 50 in practical time; head-to-head agreement is therefore established at p <= 25 and the high-p story is internal (CPU vs GPU).
GPU paths are fp32; for applications needing fp64 covariance to full precision, use the CPU backend.
Assumes missing-at-random; the estimator does not model a missingness mechanism.
The MLE requires the observed-data covariance to be non-degenerate; near-collinear columns make the problem ill-conditioned (the paper's data curation screens |corr| near 1).

datasets.name: WVS
datasets.what: World Values Survey — continuous/ordinal items, ~97k respondents, item-level missingness; large real survey with many missingness patterns.

datasets.name: GSS
datasets.what: General Social Survey — ~75k respondents; fewer but structurally different missingness patterns than WVS.
